before.title: 1.2 PureTech (EB2) Wet Timing Belt Degradation & Oil Starvation
before.description: Grandland X models with the 1.2 PureTech three-cylinder petrol engine (EB2/EB2ADTS, developed by PSA) use a 'wet' timing belt that runs submerged in engine oil. The belt coating breaks down over time, shedding rubber/material debris into the oil. This debris clogs the oil pump pickup strainer, VVT solenoids and oil passages, causing oil starvation and accelerated wear, and the belt can ultimately snap, causing catastrophic engine damage on this interference engine. Symptoms include rattling on cold start, oil/CEL warnings, ticking from the timing case and excessive oil consumption.
before.solution: Replace the wet timing belt well ahead of the original interval. Manufacturer guidance was revised down from ~180,000 km to roughly every 90,000-100,000 km (or 6 years); some specialists recommend even earlier inspection. Use only the correct low-SAPS oil and keep to short oil-change intervals to slow belt breakdown. If debris/oil starvation has occurred, the oil pump strainer, solenoids and possibly the engine must be inspected/replaced.
symptoms: Loss of power or sudden engine failure

citations.title: Why Does the Peugeot 1.2 Puretech Fail So Often? - GT Automotive
Wet Timing Belt Wear Check on 1.2 PureTech (Peugeot/Citroen/Vauxhall/Opel) - YouTube

That announcement does not identify every 2019-2024 Grandland, prove the frozen EB2/EB2ADTS equipment scope, or support the complete debris, VVT, oil-starvation, warning and catastrophic-outcome sequence for this model population.
proposal.solution: Identify the exact engine generation and timing-drive design from the VIN and current Opel/Vauxhall service information. Follow the specified oil and maintenance plan, document any oil-pressure warning or visible belt concern, and ask an authorized repairer to assess Stellantis support eligibility before work. Stop driving if an oil-pressure warning appears. Do not buy a belt kit, strainer, solenoid or engine from this page; generation, diagnosis and exact VIN fitment must be established first.

oil-pressure warning treated as a stop condition
maintenance history retained for support eligibility

before.title: Diesel SCR/AdBlue & NOx Sensor Emissions Fault with 'Starting Impossible' Limp Mode
before.description: Diesel Grandland X models (1.5 BlueHDi/1.6 diesel with SCR after-treatment) frequently throw exhaust after-treatment faults. Owners see emissions warnings, reduced power/limp mode, and the countdown message 'Engine start prevented in XXX miles/km'. Common root causes are NOx sensor failure (range/performance faults), SCR system or AdBlue injector/pump faults, crystallised AdBlue, or poor-quality urea. If ignored, the car eventually refuses to start. Critical phase is commonly around 30,000-45,000 km.
before.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool to identify whether the fault is a NOx sensor, the SCR/AdBlue dosing system, or sensor wiring/connector corrosion. Typical fixes: replace the failed NOx sensor (upstream/downstream), clean or replace the AdBlue injector/pump, refill with quality AdBlue, and clear the codes/reset the countdown. Software updates from Stellantis exist for some after-treatment faults. Do not ignore the 'start prevented' countdown.

citations.title: Grandland X Emissions Fault Starting Impossible - Vauxhall Owners Network
Opel AdBlue System Issues and Solutions - otoideal

proposal.title: Diesel SCR/AdBlue & NOx Sensor Emissions Fault with 'Starting Impossible' Limp Mode

before.title: EAT8 (Aisin AWF8) Automatic Transmission Jerking, Hesitation & Whining Noise
before.description: Grandland X models fitted with the Aisin EAT8 8-speed automatic (shared across the Stellantis/PSA platform with Peugeot/Citroen) exhibit poor low-speed shift quality once the gearbox is at operating temperature. Owners report gears 1-3 shifting very slowly with an extra throttle/RPM surge between shifts, jerking when pulling away from a stop, hesitation on kick-down, and harsh shifts when cold. A separate but common complaint is a loud metallic 'singing'/whining noise from the gearbox between roughly 45-65 km/h. Root cause is sensitivity of the EAT8 to learned adaptation values and (for the noise) gear/bearing tolerances dealers often dismiss as 'normal'.
before.solution: First step is a transmission adaptation reset followed by relearn drive cycle, plus any Opel/Stellantis transmission control software update; many cars improve significantly without mechanical repair. Persistent harsh shifting can require an ATF fluid level/quality check and service (the EAT8 needs the correct Aisin spec fluid). The whine is harder to resolve and sometimes requires valve body or gearbox replacement under warranty if severe.

before.title: Front Lower Suspension Arm Ball Joint Bolt Failure (Recall KQG)
before.description: A safety recall affects the front lower suspension arms: the fixing screws on the front left and right ball joint mounts on the front lower control arms may break. If two screws are missing the ball joint mount can pivot, allowing the affected wheel to change direction and strike the wheel arch/mudguard, compromising steering control and creating a serious accident risk. The campaign spans the shared Stellantis platform (also Peugeot 3008/5008).
before.solution: Have the recall carried out free of charge at an authorized Opel/Vauxhall dealer; technicians inspect and replace the suspension arm fixing screws/ball joint mount to the correct specification and torque. Owners noticing front-end clunking or knocking should have it inspected immediately.

before.title: IntelliLink/NAC Infotainment Freezing & Reversing Camera Dropout
before.description: Grandland X owners widely report infotainment problems: the IntelliLink/NAC head unit freezes, crashes or reboots, loses smartphone (Apple CarPlay/Android Auto) connectivity, and the reversing camera image goes black or dark intermittently. Issues often begin around 12,000-25,000 km. The reversing-camera blackout sometimes self-resolves after locking the car and leaving it, pointing to a software/module fault rather than a wiring break.
before.solution: Apply the latest infotainment/NAC software update from Opel/Vauxhall, which resolves many freeze and connectivity bugs. Persistent reversing-camera dropouts can require reseating/repairing the camera connector or replacing the camera or head unit if a hardware fault is confirmed. A battery disconnect/module reset is a common temporary workaround.
symptoms: Loss of Apple CarPlay / Android Auto connection
Reversing camera image black or intermittent

before.title: Plug-in Hybrid High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk (Recall KT8/KC5)
before.description: Grandland X Hybrid/Hybrid4 plug-in models use a 13.2 kWh lithium-ion high-voltage battery that is the subject of multiple Stellantis safety recalls. Water can infiltrate the battery case/support and cause corrosion, and a faulty high-voltage battery can overheat, creating a risk of the battery or vehicle catching fire. EU Safety Gate alert classifies this as a 'serious' defect. This is part of a wider Stellantis PHEV campaign affecting tens of thousands of vehicles across brands.
before.solution: Take the vehicle to an authorized Opel/Vauxhall dealer to have the recall performed: technicians inspect the HV battery, add water drainage holes in the battery support/reinforcement to prevent water pooling and corrosion, and replace the battery if found defective. Until repaired, some campaigns advise limiting charging. Repair is free of charge under the recall.
symptoms: Risk of fire/smoke from battery area

citations.title: Recall: Opel Grandland X (2019-2021) EV/Hybrid fire - car-recalls.eu
